slides.title: Used by:
slides.text:
Used by:


JPMorgan- Calculating various outcomes and risks that come with investing
Microsoft- Trying to make fertilizer better but the computer produces so much greenhouse gas.
Rigetti Computing- Predict better weather patterns
ProteinQure- Molecular simulation of protein behavior. Checks how proteins are engineered for more targeted medicine
Daimler Truck AG- Working on making car batteries for EV and more sustainable batteries.
Infleqtion- Make error-corrected Qubits and Quantum Computers. By using laser-cooled atoms that can play the roles of qubits.

slides.title: Used for (cont.):
slides.text:
Used for (cont.):  

Batteries- Can help look into how we can make batteries last longer and increase the efficiency by understanding the docking energies.
Manufacturing/Testing- Making test models more accurate to where they require less testing.
Traffic Optimization- Can use weather and real time traffic patterns/alerts to find better and faster routes to help with the flow of the supply chain, logistics and transportation.
AI/ML- Can help implement AI/ML into applications at a much larger scale
Material Science- Can be used to stimulate the strength of various materials which helps cut down on costs and time by pretesting the materials durability before using it.

slides.title: Limitations:
slides.text:
Limitations:  

Super expensive to afford so only big companies can afford them
They are VERY sensitive to their environments like heat, vibration etc.
Difficult to calibrate because of the infinite number of qubits
Data can be corrupted due to buildup off errors, imperfected software's/hardware, and the qubits interacting with their environment.
Don’t have the best software's to handle what we need them to do and requires very specific knowledge of quantum programming and mechanics.
